title: ARD section 1 - Models (model motions)

container.notes: ARD section 1 (models / model motions; u32 count + 8-byte rows; stored LAST in the ARD with nothing after it). ARD = standalone *.ard or section 19 of an .ebp: 8-byte magic FF12AR03, ten u32 section offsets at 0x08 relative to the ARD start (0 = absent; this section = u32 at ARD+0x0C); sections 0,2..9 written in index order on 16-byte boundaries with zero fill, section 1 written last with nothing after it. A section spans to the next larger non-zero offset (the highest to the end of the ARD).

records.name: modelsHeader
records.where: Offset 0 of ARD section 1 (ARD start + u32 at ARD+0x0C).

fields.name: entryCount
fields.notes: Number of 8-byte model rows that follow immediately (no st2e header, no gap).

fields.name: model
fields.notes: Model id = (ASCII prefix letter << 16) | file number (foes use prefix m, TK L940-L952).

fields.name: unknownFlags
fields.notes: Flag word of unknown meaning. The Toolkit calls the section "Model Motions" (motion sets per model), so it may select motion data. Keep as found.

roundTrip: Keep section 1 as the physically last section of the ARD and write nothing after it.
Values are edited in place; the 8-byte rows have no internal offsets.
Keep the bytes after the last row (padding, EBP padding) exactly as found when the row count does not change.
When rows are added or removed, update entryCount, re-pad to 16 with zeros, and fix the ARD total length / enclosing EBP offsets (no other ARD offset moves).
Keep unknownFlags verbatim unless you know what you are changing.
gaps: Meaning of the u32 flag word in each row (possibly motion-set selection, per the Toolkit's "Model Motions" label).
Why the game requires section 1 to be stored last (possibly so it can be released or grown separately after loading).
Whether vanilla ARDs pad section 1 to 16 bytes; the Workshop always does.
Whether every model referenced by classes, overlays or special action animations must be present in this list.
Order significance of the rows (nothing is known to index them).
